How It Works

Five ways agentic AI shows up in sustainability.

Click any step to see it in more depth.

Agents pull activity data — fuel logs, utility bills, fleet telematics, procurement records — directly from ERPs and meters, mapping it to Scope 1, 2, and 3 categories without manual spreadsheet consolidation.

Continuous monitoring flags unexplained spikes in electricity, water, or gas consumption at the site or asset level, surfacing leaks, equipment faults, or data errors within days instead of at year-end audit.

Agents run and compare abatement pathways — electrification, on-site solar, efficiency retrofits — against capex, energy prices, and projected carbon costs to rank interventions by cost per tonne abated.

Disclosure narratives and data tables for frameworks like IFRS S1/S2, CSRD-aligned supplier requests, or ADX ESG guidance are drafted automatically from verified data, leaving sustainability teams to review rather than compile.

Agents track supplier disclosures, certifications, and news signals continuously, flagging deteriorating risk or missing data before it becomes a compliance gap in your Scope 3 inventory.
